scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs weighing consequences before risk while granting that some moments demand fast action; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Every important choice in life carries some risk, from starting a business to crossing a busy road.
Some people recommend that a person should undertake risky action only after carefully considering its consequences.
I largely agree that thinking before acting is wise, but I believe demanding full consideration before every risk would sometimes do more harm than good.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why considering consequences is wise

sentences.text: First, in most situations, weighing the consequences before taking a risk is plainly sensible.
Careful thought helps people avoid the disasters that a single moment of recklessness might cause.
For example, a person who studies the dangers before investing her savings is far less likely to lose everything.
This shows that thinking ahead can turn a reckless gamble into a reasonable, calculated decision.
People who act without considering the results often regret choices they could easily have avoided.
Considering consequences also helps us prepare for problems instead of being caught by surprise.
For these reasons, careful thought should usually come before any risky action.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why some risks need fast action

sentences.text: Second, however, insisting on full consideration before every risk would itself cause problems.
Some opportunities and emergencies demand fast action, leaving no time for long and careful thought.
Consider a person who must decide in mere seconds whether to pull a stranger out of danger.
Such moments show that endless caution can cost us valuable chances and even lives.
Many great achievements also required people to take bold risks before every outcome was known.
If we waited to understand every consequence, we might never act, invent, or explore at all.
Some risks, then, are worth taking even without complete certainty.
In conclusion, carefully considering consequences is usually a wise habit before taking a risk.
But demanding full certainty before every action would leave us frozen and afraid.
The best approach is to think carefully when we can, while staying ready to act boldly when we must.
